# Step split screen — Style Prompt

> The classic half-and-half tutorial reel. The top half is warm paper with a faint dot grid: a small orange step badge, a big light serif headline with one word in orange italic, and a white app window under it that acts out exactly what the speaker says, at the word they say it (a cursor picks one tile, a button presses, a checklist ticks). The bottom half is the speaker's own footage, eyes about 300 px below the seam. Bold uppercase captions in a dark pill sit right on the seam, each word brightening as it is spoken. One step per beat, numbered "Langkah 1, 2, 3".

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

1. **The window shows what the words say, when they say it.** The cursor clicks on "pilih", the button presses on "klik", a row ticks on its keyword. Nothing in the window moves without a word behind it.
2. **One step per beat.** The badge numbers it; the headline names it in 3-5 words; the window proves it. A series is several beats (or several reels), never two steps in one window.
3. **The speaker is half the frame and never covered.** Graphics stay in the top half; only the caption pill crosses the seam.
4. **Calm paper, one loud colour.** The orange belongs to the badge, the italic word, the pick ring, the ticks and the pressed button.

Not a full-screen screen recording (the face is always there). Not a picture-in-picture bubble. Not a slideshow: the window is a live app with a cursor, not a static card. Not a meme split (no reaction faces, no shake, no zoom punches on the speaker).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Top half (0-960 px)**: `--latar` paper with a dot grid (1.6 px dots every 36 px at 8 % of the ink), drawn once as a CSS background.
- **Badge**: a 16 px-radius pill in `--utama`, padding 12/26/12/20, a 12-ray star (40 px) before the text, a soft coloured shadow (0 10 24, 35 %).
- **Window**: 860 × 520 px, radius 30, `--latar-2`, shadow 0 30 70 at 18 % ink plus a 1 px hairline; a 78 px bar with three traffic-light dots (16 px) and a 46 px search pill (`--teks` 5 % on the window) holding a lens icon and the query in 25 px.
- **Inside the window**, one of three: a **grid** (4 columns of 190 × 238 tiles, radius 10, 14 px gaps) of the user's images with small green count chips; a **checklist** (up to 4 rows of 96 px, a 58 px rounded box per row); a **screenshot** (the user's page, panning). Tiles and screenshots are the user's own images from `list_media`; the example paints food-photo stand-ins with gradients.
- **Pick ring**: a 5 px `--utama` border, radius 14, around the chosen tile, which scales to 1.1 while the others drop to 35 %. **Fan**: three 150 × 188 slides fly out of the picked tile, rotated -8°/0°/+8°.
- **Button**: a dark pill (`--tombol`), 32 px bold, that flashes to `--utama` when pressed. **Cursor**: a dark arrow with a white edge, 46 px.
- **Bottom half (960-1920 px)**: the speaker's clip full width, moved up so the eyes sit about y 1260 (`top = 300 − eye y` in the clip's 1080 × 1920 frame); the chin stays above y 1500.
- **Caption pill**: radius 24, padding 18/34/20, `--pil` near-black with a deep shadow; text 66 px uppercase.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar` is the paper of the top half; `--latar-2` the window and its contents' ground.
- `--utama` is the one loud colour: the badge, the pick ring, the filled check boxes, the pressed button. Its text is `--teks-di-utama`.
- `--utama-di-latar` colours the italic headline word and the italic keyword in each checklist row.
- `--aksen` is the green of count chips and result labels (`--teks-di-aksen` on it); `--aksen-di-latar` for green words on the window (sold counts).
- `--teks` is the headline and window text; `--teks-redup` the search query, subtitles and labels.
- Fixed in every brand: the caption pill (`--pil`, `--pil-teks`) because it sits on footage, the dark button and cursor (`--tombol`), the three window dots, and the colours of the user's images (`--p1…--p8` in the example). The footage is never recoloured.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` carries the badge (44 px, 400), the headline (96 px, 400, line-height 1, −0.01em, one line, centred, one word in italic) and the checklist keywords (italic 50 px). The example uses Instrument Serif (an open font library, roman and italic), a light, narrow display serif; Cormorant Garamond or Playfair Display also suit. A wide brand serif needs a shorter headline (≤ 22 characters).
- `--font-isi` carries captions (66 px, 800, uppercase, +0.01em), checklist rows (40 px, 600), the button (32 px, 800), chips (22 px, 800), the search query (25 px, 600). Inter in the example.
- Captions: at most 4 words or 16 characters per pill, one line, no punctuation, uppercase.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Beat entry** (each step): the window rises 50 px and fades in over 0.4 s `power3.out`; the badge and headline rise 20 px over 0.35 s, 0.08 s apart, from the same moment. Hard cut between steps.
- **Grid pick**: the grid scrolls up 150 px `power1.inOut` until the cursor moves; chips pop 0 → 1 in 0.2 s `back.out(2.5)`, 0.035 s apart, on the word that counts them; the cursor travels 0.55 s `power2.inOut` and arrives 0.66 s before the pick word; the click is a 0.07 s squeeze to 0.82 and back; the others dim to 35 % and the tile scales to 1.1 `back.out(2)` in 0.25 s; the ring fades in over 0.15 s.
- **Button**: rises 20 px from 0.9 scale in 0.24 s `back.out(2)` on its word; the cursor glides 0.32 s to it; on the click word it squeezes to 0.95 and flashes `--utama` in 0.1 s; the fan follows 0.12 s later, each slide 0.3 s `power3.out`, 0.05 s apart.
- **Checklist**: each row slides in 30 px over 0.3 s `power3.out`, 0.35 s before its keyword; on the keyword the box fills in 0.15 s and pops 1.25 → 1 in 0.25 s `back.out(3)`.
- **Screenshot**: pans 120-260 px over the whole beat, `power1.inOut`.
- **Captions**: each pill appears 0.04 s before its first word, pops 0.92 → 1 in 0.12 s `back.out(2)`; words sit at 42 % and turn full white 0.02 s before they are spoken; the pill stays until the next one.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Static split, speaker locked in the bottom half | "follow along", the teacher is right here | every beat |
| Window rise (50 px, 0.4 s) on a hard cut | the next step starts | each new step of a tutorial, a recipe, a setup |
| Grid scroll then cursor pick | searching, then choosing | picking a reference, a product, a template |
| Button press with a fan of slides | the action produces something | exporting, ordering, generating a result |
| Checklist ticking word by word | preparing, ticking off | ingredients, tools, a setup routine |
| Slow screenshot pan | here is the result, look around | a shop page, a dashboard, a finished design |

No zooms or shakes on the speaker; the footage only moves if the user's own camera moves.

## 7. Native moves

- **Numbered step badge + one italic word.** "Langkah 1" in the pill, then "Cari foto yang *laku*". *Fits content like:* a baker's three-step photo routine; a teacher's "Langkah 2: Tulis *kerangka*"; a creator's editing series; a barber's "Langkah 3: Rapikan *tengkuk*".
- **Grid pick.** Tiles scroll, chips pop on the number word, the cursor picks one on "pilih", the rest dim, a button presses and slides fan out. *Fits content like:* choosing a best-selling product photo; picking a template; choosing a reference video to copy; a librarian picking the book of the week.
- **Ticking checklist.** Up to four rows, each ticking orange as it is said, keyword in italic serif. *Fits content like:* what to prepare before a shoot; a packing list; a class's homework; the ingredients of a recipe.
- **Panning proof.** The result as a screenshot in the window, a green label pops on the word that names the gain. *Fits content like:* a shop page after the change; a student's finished essay; a channel's analytics; a booking calendar filling up.
- **Seam captions.** A dark uppercase pill straddling the seam, each word lighting as spoken. *Fits content like:* every beat; it is the look's voice.

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Anything happening before its word.** Anchor every action to a word's start in the transcript (`inspect_media` gives words `{text, start, end}`); the headline and badge are the only things there from the first frame of a beat.
- **Covering the face.** The window ends 30 px above the seam; only the caption pill crosses it. If the eyes sit higher or lower in the user's clip, move the clip (`top = 300 − eye y`), never the graphics; keep the chin above y 1500 and the headline below y 220 (platform UI zones).
- **Long headlines.** One line at 96 px (≈ 22 characters in a narrow serif). Two steps in one headline means two beats.
- **Made-up numbers.** Chips and counts come from the user; if they gave none, leave chips out.
- **Captions longer than 4 words or 16 characters**, or with punctuation: split them.
- **Performance**: the grid, slides and screenshot are images or gradients moved by transforms; no blur, no animated shadows.

## 9. Using the user's footage

- Footage: `<video src="assets/media/upl_….mp4" data-start data-duration data-media-start data-track-index muted>` from `list_media`, 1080 px wide inside the bottom half, `top = 300 − eye y` (read the eye line from `inspect_media`'s frames). A landscape clip is reframed to a vertical crop first (craft `reframe.md`): keep the face centred horizontally.
- Its sound is the voice; the window and captions follow its transcript. Build caption pills from the transcript words: 4 words or 16 characters per pill, lowercase source words shown uppercase, the pill from its first word's start − 0.04 s to the next pill's.
- No cutout is needed in this look: nothing passes behind the speaker.
- 16:9: the window goes to the left half (same 860 × 520 window, headline 96 px), the speaker fills the right half with the eyes about y 400, and the caption pill sits low across the vertical seam.

# Step split screen: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 3, medium 4, long 5.

## hook

- en: Langkah 1 badge, serif headline with one italic word; the window acts out the first action on its word (grid pick + button)
- id: lencana Langkah 1, judul serif dengan satu kata miring; jendela memperagakan aksi pertama tepat pada katanya (pilih grid + tombol)

## problem

- en: window shows the mess as the speaker names it: a screenshot of the bad state panning slowly, a label pops on the word
- id: jendela menunjukkan masalahnya saat disebut: tangkapan layar keadaan buruk digeser pelan, label muncul pada katanya

## fact

- en: badge + headline state the fact; the window holds one screenshot or card that proves it, panning
- id: lencana + judul menyebut faktanya; jendela berisi satu tangkapan layar atau kartu buktinya, digeser pelan

## step

- en: next Langkah N badge; a checklist in the window ticks orange on each keyword, or the cursor clicks what is said
- id: lencana Langkah N berikutnya; ceklis di jendela tercentang oranye pada tiap kata kunci, atau kursor mengklik yang disebut

## compare

- en: the window's grid: all tiles shown, the cursor picks the better one on its word, the others dim to 35%
- id: grid di jendela: semua ubin tampil, kursor memilih yang lebih baik pada katanya, sisanya meredup 35%

## number

- en: the number lands as a green chip on the tiles (or a big label in the window) on the word that says it
- id: angkanya mendarat sebagai chip hijau di ubin (atau label besar di jendela) pada kata yang menyebutnya

## proof

- en: the result as a screenshot panning in the window, a green result label pops on the gain word
- id: hasilnya sebagai tangkapan layar yang digeser di jendela, label hasil hijau muncul pada kata keuntungannya

## offer

- en: the product or class as a card in the window, price in the headline's italic word, the button pops on its word
- id: produk atau kelas sebagai kartu di jendela, harga di kata miring judul, tombol muncul pada katanya

## cta

- en: a card with the contact in the window, the cursor presses the button on the ask word, held 2 s
- id: kartu kontak di jendela, kursor menekan tombol pada kata ajakan, diam 2 dtk

## payoff

- en: back to the finished result in the window, the headline names the win, captions end on the seam, held 2 s
- id: kembali ke hasil jadi di jendela, judul menyebut hasilnya, caption terakhir di sambungan, diam 2 dtk
